title: Malvern Dowsers explore asteroid Chiron in public talk
excerpt: Local astrologer Robin Higgins led the Malvern Dowsers’ final public talk of the year, exploring the significance of the planetoid Chiron and its place in astrology.
content:
Malvern Dowsers discuss astrology and asteroid Chiron

Robin Higgins led the Malvern Dowsers’ final public talk of the year (Image: Supplied)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

The Malvern Dowsers concluded their public talks with a discussion on the asteroid Chiron.

Local astrologer Robin Higgins led the session, explaining the significance of Chiron, a planetoid discovered in 1977.

Named after a wounded healer and teacher from ancient Greek mythology, Chiron is a planetoid body of rock and ice already popular with astrologers.

Mr Higgins used his own birth chart to demonstrate how Chiron's position will affect a whole generation of young people.

The Malvern Dowsers will continue after Christmas on Zoom for members.

They plan to resume live public talks and events in Malvern next spring.
